original_question: If X is a well-filtered determined T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) also well-filtered determined? Here PS(X) is the upper Vietoris space on the nonempty compact saturated subsets of X.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Question 6.5: "Is the Smyth power space P_S(X) of a well-filtered determined T0 space X well-filtered determined?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target almost verbatim: it has the correct hypothesis (X is a well-filtered determined T0 space), the correct construction (the Smyth power space P_S(X)), and the correct conclusion being asked about (whether P_S(X) is again well-filtered determined). It also correctly identifies P_S(X) as the upper Vietoris space on the nonempty compact saturated subsets of X.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem, specifically Question 6.5 in Section 6, not as a theorem or conjecture.
To make the question fully stand-alone, 'well-filtered determined' should be unpacked: a T0 space Z is well-filtered determined iff every irreducible closed subset A of Z is a WD set.

A WD set A is defined via continuous maps into well-filtered spaces: for every continuous map f: Z -> Y into a well-filtered T0 space Y, there exists a unique y_A in Y such that cl_Y(f(A)) = cl_Y({y_A}), where cl_Y denotes closure in Y.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether this holds for every well-filtered determined T0 space X.

If one wants the definition of P_S(X) to be fully explicit, one should say that P_S(X)=K(X) with K(X) the set of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of X, endowed with the upper Vietoris topology generated by the basic opens square(U)={K in K(X) : K subseteq U} for U open in X.

Paper-faithful nearby context includes Theorem 6.4, which proves the reverse implication P_S(X) well-filtered determined => X well-filtered determined, so the unresolved issue is exactly whether well-filtered determinedness is preserved by the Smyth power space construction.
The immediately preceding Theorem 6.2 shows the analogous equivalence for well-filteredness itself, which explains why Question 6.5 is posed in this section.
refined_question: For every T0 space X that is well-filtered determined, in the sense that every irreducible closed subset A of X is a WD set (equivalently, for every continuous map f: X -> Y into any well-filtered T0 space Y there exists a unique y_A in Y with cl_Y(f(A)) = cl_Y({y_A})), must its Smyth power space P_S(X) = K(X), where K(X) is the set of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of X equipped with the upper Vietoris topology generated by the basic opens square(U) = {K in K(X) : K subseteq U} for U open in X, also be a well-filtered determined space?
justification: The draft is trying to capture exactly Question 6.5 in Section 6, and its wording is already very close to the official formulation. The notation P_S(X) and the upper Vietoris construction are fixed earlier in Section 2, while the meaning of 'well-filtered determined' is supplied in Definition 5.5 of Section 5. The nearby Theorem 6.4 proves the converse implication from the Smyth power space back to X, and Theorem 6.2 just above records the corresponding preservation/reflection result for well-filteredness itself. So the sharp paper-faithful standalone version is the same Question 6.5, with the WD definition spelled out explicitly.
